message.content: **Summary:** I researched Apple's most recent results and news, then bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.90 (filled at $222.90, ~$9,808 total), which is within a few cents of the current quote of $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72) and comfortably inside the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps; no funds were moved out of the account, and the only other position (100 MSFT shares) was left untouched. The decision rested on Apple's fiscal Q4 2024 report (quarterly revenue of $94.9B, up 6% year over year) and the FY2024 10-K figures: total net sales of $391,035M (up from $383,285M), operating income of $123,216M, net income of $93,736M, and diluted EPS of $6.08 — noting that net income and EPS were depressed by a one-time $10.2B income tax charge, so underlying profitability was stronger than the headline decline from $96,995M / $6.13 suggests. News flow was neutral-to-mildly positive: shares were steady around $222 as investors weighed iPhone 16 demand and the gradual Apple Intelligence rollout, which is a reasonable entry point rather than a clear catalyst, so I sized the position modestly (about 20% of available cash) rather than committing the full daily allowance.
